We would try to guess these things; that's how it was in those days, because people spoke very often on those frequencies. Very often the conversations were of a private nature and we only recorded what we deemed relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just let me try to get this right again, when I said "decipher," I did not mean in the technical sense of the word. Did you sort of talk to each other and try to help each other out to hear more clearly what had been recorded in the process of transcribing an intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: That was when we typed it. That's when we did it. When the conversation was actually being received, there was just one person taking it down in order to register the fact that it was received and recorded. That's what it was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about this? Could it happen, for example, that the person typing it up or transcribing a conversation added words, words which may have been synonyms and yet changed the meaning of the sentence all together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: Well, what can I say? This person was also a ham radio operator and he knew about encryption and coding. It was up to that person what he did, but I'm sure they all did their best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Generally speaking, this may have been the case, but you couldn't know that, could you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This may have been the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that would have been perfectly possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just several questions left. You said that you had at one point begun to recognise some of the voices appearing on the frequencies. You referred to General Krstic, to Jevdjevic, to Pandurevic. What I want to know is the following: Were you ever in a situation where you recognised the voice of an officer named Jokic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't remember. I don't remember his voice. Now I can't recall his voice; back then, maybe, but I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just one question. In view of the newly arisen differences or discrepancies between the interceptions made at Okresanica and Konjuh respectively, in relation to the same conversation, was it ever the case that you were trying to improve the quality of your work, Okresanica and Konjuh, and that you would meet to listen to intercepts together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: Not for as long as I was there, this never happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about platoon commanders, sometimes they would try to improve the quality and they would meet up perhaps to see if there was any errors being committed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-121
utterances.text: I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour. I would like to use this opportunity to thank the witness, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, are there any documents to tender at this stage? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage, we're tendering P352, which is the pseudonym sheet. And I just again echo what I indicated earlier, we will be tendering the intercepts and notebooks after the last witness testifies, which I believe will be Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I guess there's no objections from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour, and I have nothing to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours, no objections. It was for these very reasons that we wanted to verify that particular piece of information, because the way we speak, we always throw the letter J in, but I think that's settled now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document is admitted into the evidence. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence, and all of us will wish you a pleasant journey back home tomorrow. And when we withdraw, the usher will show out of the room. Yes, the hearing is adjourned until Monday morning.
